host.cpu: AMD 3020e with Radeon Graphics, 2 cores, 1 thread per core, no P/E split; acpi-cpufreq 800/1000/1200 MHz + boost to 2594 MHz
host.compositor: Hyprland 0.56.2, native Wayland client (wayland 1.26.0), temporary headless output QA at 60 Hz
host.pinning: app under taskset -c 1 (all threads), driver pinned to CPU 0; P-core pinning does not apply (no P/E split)
host.frequency_hold: R1, R2: a SCHED_IDLE busy loop on CPU 1 (taskset -c 1 chrt -i 0) held CPU 1 at 2544-2594 MHz in every sample; it yields to every normal task. R3, R4: none, schedutil moves CPU 1 between 690 and 2594 MHz.
host.cache: fresh HOME/XDG per launch (Mesa/RADV shader caches cold at launch, removed after); OS page cache warm (fixture read by every launch); 20 unrecorded warm-up notches per launch
host.other_load: owner desktop session and agent processes; load average 0.3-1.7 across runs (per launch in launches[])

configs.wide: 1480x800 fullscreen, scale 1: labelled scope toolbar in both builds (toolbar strip pixel-identical)
configs.narrow: 461x490 tiled beside a foot window on a 1920x1080 scale-2 output: candidate draws the compact toolbar (icons only), base the labelled toolbar clipped

procedure: per launch: 6 s settle, pointer on the History list (0.3,0.6 wide; 0.3,0.78 narrow) with the app verified as the active window, 20 warm-up notches, 20 idle windows, 120 recorded wheel notches (30 down, 30 up, 30 down, 30 up) from a zwlr_virtual_pointer_v1, one every 150 ms, 20 idle windows. No keys. SIGTERM by PID.

metrics.scene_ms: wl_pointer.frame closing the notch, as dispatched in the app (libwayland WAYLAND_DEBUG log), to the app's next wl_surface.frame request, which WaylandWindow::draw issues once Window::draw has built the scene: scroll dispatch, root render with render_history and its scope toolbar, layout, prepaint, paint. Parked sample: the frame loop was parked (no wl_callback.done between event and request, one frame drawn), so the draw ran from the loop's ping and the 60 Hz tick grid does not enter the value. Non-parked notches (8 per narrow launch at the same indices in both builds, after a notch that drew a second frame) wait for a compositor tick and are bounded below by its phase. Excludes compositor delivery, renderer submission, GPU execution and scanout.
metrics.submit_ms: that wl_surface.frame request to the Mesa WSI's wl_surface.commit: wgpu encode, queue submit and present. Excludes GPU completion.
metrics.main_cpu_ms: main-thread on-CPU time (/proc/PID/task/PID/schedstat) over the 150 ms from just before the notch is written: dispatch, handler, the drawn frame including renderer submission, the next frame callback that finds nothing dirty, and any other main-thread work (idle windows median 0.000). CPU time: no tick-grid floor.
metrics.main_wait_ms: main-thread runqueue wait in the same window.

statistics: nearest rank (ceil(p*n)-th smallest); delta = candidate - base of the pooled statistic; ci95 from 10000 (p99: 2000) resamples of samples within each launch
